content: 1. Elagolix, when co-administered with CYP3A substrates, may reduce their plasma levels or therapeutic effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. If necessary, consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A substrate and monitor closely for clinical response and tolerability. 2. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration cannot be avoided, increase the dosing frequency of ripretinib from 150 mg once daily to 150 mg twice daily during the co-administration period. Monitor for clinical response and tolerability. 3. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of risperidone and ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Elagolix decreases the levels of ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 5. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered, and consider increasing their dose if needed. 6. Elagolix decreases the levels of rivaroxaban, roflumilast, rolapitant, romidepsin, ropivacaine, and rosuvastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. For rosuvastatin, consider increasing its dose. 7. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated and monitor closely. 8. Rufinamide decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rufinamide is a weak CYP3A4 inducer and may reduce the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. 9. Elagolix decreases the levels of ruxolitinib (both systemic and topical), salmeterol, saxagliptin, sildenafil, silodosin, simvastatin, siponimod, sirolimus, sitagliptin, sofosbuvir, solifenacin, sonidegib, sorafenib, and other CYP3A4 substrates by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 10. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. 12. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Elagolix decreases the levels of stiripentol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 13. Elagolix decreases the levels of sufentanil, sunitinib, suvorexant, tacrolimus, tadalafil, talazoparib, tamsulosin, tasimelteon, and other CYP3A4 substrates by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 14. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. 15. Telotristat ethyl decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Acetazolamide, anastrozole, cyclophosphamide, danazol, drospirenone, and larotrectinib increase the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 17. Voclosporin, an OATP1B1 inhibitor, may increase the concentration of OATP1B1 substrates, including elagolix. Monitor for adverse reactions of OATP1B1 substrates when co-administered with voclosporin. 18. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of abemaciclib, abiraterone, acalabrutinib, ado-trastuzumab emtansine, and other CYP3A4 substrates by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 19. Acitretin decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate by an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely.
